items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No code diff was captured. The 5.4KB size and identical stdout ('Analysis complete...Takeoff: frame 54') suggest the agent adapted the solve.sh it read at step [11]. That code uses cryptic positional indexing (data[:, 2], jump[8], jump[7]) and leftover names like first_frame and original_frames.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: This appears to be the copied reference pattern. extract_jump_metrics is a single function of about 100 lines with 5+ levels of nesting. It contains dead code (original_frames, an unreachable 'if first_frame is None' branch, redundant len checks) and an unused fps/skip_frames=1.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The reference-style main() catches every error with 'except Exception as e: print(...)' and then writes 0/0 placeholder output, so failures are hidden behind fake results. It never checks cap.isOpened(). Magic constants are inline (960, 15, 5, (11,11) blur kernel).

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: There is no cap.isOpened() check. When no motion is found, the ValueError is caught and fake values jump_takeoff=0 and jump_land=0 are written, with exit code 0. Thresholds are absolute pixel constants (crop_height=15, foot_width=5, video_width=960).

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: It reads argv[1] and writes /app/output.toml with exactly two integer fields (output 'jump_takeoff_frame_number = 54 / jump_land_frame_number = 63'). It falls back to a hard-coded '/app/input.mp4' when no argument is given, and the 1-based frame numbering is never stated.
